text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday.
- Local elections in the last Serb-run enclave of Eastern Slavonia will be definitely held in April and not in mid-March as it was previously scheduled, sources reveal.

- Two Croats and one Moslem reported killed in the most serious incident that happened in the divided city of Mostar since the war ended in 1995. Some 18 Croat policemen were wounded when they tried to stop the Moslem mob from entering the Croat part of the city.
- Citizens who opt to settle down in former Serb-held lands can apply for rebuilding loans of up to 44,000 kuna.
- Trains will be running on all tracks of Eastern Slavonia by May, extensive rebuilding planned.
- Talks between textile trade union and the employers' association have been suspended following the latter's refusal to approve a minimum wage of 1,200 kuna for textile workers.
- Croatia's first $300 million five-year Eurobond, launched last week, had a successful debut. Demand overshot planned issue three times.

- Serbs from Eastern Slavonia are taking away private and public property to Serbia. Some 122 loaded trucks have already left the region, says Ivica Vrkic, head of the government's reintegration office.
- "We want a speedy trial," says Anto Nobilo, defence counsel of Bosnian Croat general Tihomir Blaskic, indicted by the Hague War Crimes Tribunal.
- Editorial: Incidents provoked by Moslem in Mostar at the time Croatia is preparing for the the summer's tourist season, are more than just a provocation.
- Croatia will be the most popular destination for Czech tourists in summer 1997, a tourist trade fair in Prague showed.

- Citizens of Zagreb needed more than their average monthly wages or 2,435 kuna for basic consumer products last December. December living costs were 1.1 percent higher than the 1996 average. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
